# Lecture Notes

## Double Categories

<b>Definition 1.1</b> (Double category) <i>
A <u> double category </u> $\mathbb{C}$ consists of the following data:

1. a category $\mathbb{C}_0$, whose objects we call 0-<u>cells</u>, and whose arrows we call <u>tight</u> 1-<u> cells</u>
$f: V \rightarrow V'$;

2. a category $\mathbb{C}_1$, whose objects we call <u>loose</u> 1-<u>cells</u> $N: V \not\rightarrow W$, and whose
arrows we call 2-<u>cells</u>

::: {.imagify}
[]: % https://q.uiver.app/#q=WzAsNSxbMCwwLCJYIl0sWzIsMCwiWSJdLFswLDIsIlYiXSxbMiwyLCJXIl0sWzEsMSwiXFxEb3duYXJyb3cgXFxwaGkiXSxbMCwxLCJNIiwwLHsic3R5bGUiOnsiYm9keSI6eyJuYW1lIjoiYmFycmVkIn19fV0sWzAsMiwiZiIsMl0sWzIsMywiTiIsMix7InN0eWxlIjp7ImJvZHkiOnsibmFtZSI6ImJhcnJlZCJ9fX1dLFsxLDMsImciXV0=
\begin{tikzcd}
	V && W \\
	& {\Downarrow \phi} \\
	V' && W'
	\arrow["N"{inner sep=.8ex}, "\shortmid"{marking}, from=1-1, to=1-3]
	\arrow["f"', from=1-1, to=3-1]
	\arrow["g", from=1-3, to=3-3]
	\arrow["N'"'{inner sep=.8ex}, "\shortmid"{marking}, from=3-1, to=3-3]
\end{tikzcd}
:::

3. two functors $\text{src}, \text{tgt} : \mathbb{C}_1 \rightarrow \mathbb{C}_0$ called <u>source</u>
and <u>target</u> respectively;

4. <u>composition</u> and <u>identity</u> functors $\text{comp} : \mathbb{C}_1 \times_{\mathbb{C}_0} \mathbb{C}_1$ and $\text{id} : \mathbb{C}_0 \rightarrow \mathbb{C}_1$;

5. natural families of globular isomorphisms in $\mathbb{C}_1$:

::: {.imagify}
[]: %
\begin{tikzcd}
	V && Y \\
	& {\Downarrow a_{P,M,N}} \\
	V && Y
	\arrow["(P\circ M) \circ N"{inner sep=.8ex}, "\shortmid"{marking}, from=1-1, to=1-3]
	\arrow[equals, nfold, from=1-1, to=3-1]
	\arrow[equals, nfold, from=1-3, to=3-3]
	\arrow["P \circ (M \circ N)"'{inner sep=.8ex}, "\shortmid"{marking}, from=3-1, to=3-3]
\end{tikzcd}
:::

::: {.imagify}
[]: %
\begin{tikzcd}
	W && X \\
	& {\Downarrow \ell_M} \\
	W && X
	\arrow["\text{id}_X \circ M"{inner sep=.8ex}, "\shortmid"{marking}, from=1-1, to=1-3]
	\arrow[equals, nfold, from=1-1, to=3-1]
	\arrow[equals, nfold, from=1-3, to=3-3]
	\arrow["M"'{inner sep=.8ex}, "\shortmid"{marking}, from=3-1, to=3-3]
\end{tikzcd}
:::

::: {.imagify}
[]: %
\begin{tikzcd}
	W && X \\
	& {\Downarrow r_M} \\
	W && X
	\arrow["M \circ \text{id}_W"{inner sep=.8ex}, "\shortmid"{marking}, from=1-1, to=1-3]
	\arrow[equals, nfold, from=1-1, to=3-1]
	\arrow[equals, nfold, from=1-3, to=3-3]
	\arrow["M"'{inner sep=.8ex}, "\shortmid"{marking}, from=3-1, to=3-3]
\end{tikzcd}
:::


These data are required to satisfy the following coherence axioms which manifest as equations between composite 2-cells.

The first of these is the following composite

::: {.imagify}
[]: %
\begin{tikzcd}
	V && Z \\
	& {\Downarrow a_{Q, P, M} \star \text{id}_N} \\
	V && Z\\
    & {\Downarrow a_{Q, P \circ M, N} }\\
    V && Z \\
    & {\Downarrow id_Q \star a_{P, M, N} }\\
    V && Z
	\arrow["((Q \circ P)\circ N) \circ M"{inner sep=.8ex}, "\shortmid"{marking}, from=1-1, to=1-3]
	\arrow[equals, nfold, from=1-1, to=3-1]
	\arrow[equals, nfold, from=1-3, to=3-3]
	\arrow["(Q \circ (P \circ M)) \circ N"'{inner sep=.8ex}, "\shortmid"{marking}, from=3-1, to=3-3]
	\arrow[equals, nfold, from=3-1, to=5-1]
	\arrow[equals, nfold, from=3-3, to=5-3]
	\arrow["Q \circ ((P \circ M) \circ N)"'{inner sep=.8ex}, "\shortmid"{marking}, from=5-1, to=5-3]
	\arrow[equals, nfold, from=5-1, to=7-1]
	\arrow[equals, nfold, from=5-3, to=7-3]
	\arrow["Q \circ (P \circ (M \circ N))"'{inner sep=.8ex}, "\shortmid"{marking}, from=7-1, to=7-3]
\end{tikzcd}
:::

which is required to be equal to the second composite

::: {.imagify}
[]: %
\begin{tikzcd}
	V && Z \\
	& {\Downarrow a_{Q \circ P, M, N}} \\
	V && Z\\
    & {\Downarrow a_{Q, P, M \circ N} }\\
    V && Z \\
	\arrow["((Q \circ P)\circ N) \circ M"{inner sep=.8ex}, "\shortmid"{marking}, from=1-1, to=1-3]
	\arrow[equals, nfold, from=1-1, to=3-1]
	\arrow[equals, nfold, from=1-3, to=3-3]
	\arrow["(Q \circ P) \circ (M \circ N)"'{inner sep=.8ex}, "\shortmid"{marking}, from=3-1, to=3-3]
	\arrow[equals, nfold, from=3-1, to=5-1]
	\arrow[equals, nfold, from=3-3, to=5-3]
	\arrow["Q \circ ((P \circ M) \circ N)"'{inner sep=.8ex}, "\shortmid"{marking}, from=5-1, to=5-3]
\end{tikzcd}
:::


</i>
